label: Modal spine A3′: pricing the non-well-founded-past and never-generated horns
summary: Target: the two horns left to the initial-state view by ContingentComingToBe.possibleContingentFreePast (attempt 59ac4727). In every accessible history either (H1) some contingent concrete thing was never preceded by its own absence, or (H2) no moment with a contingent concrete thing present has a founded past. Spec: specs/modal-spine-coming-to-be-horns.toml. Revised after the independent semantic challenge and Codex review of PR 1463. H2 MEANING: founded is Acc of the strict order of moments, so H2 is a non-well-founded populated past. It covers an endless past and also a dense past with a first moment (on non-negative rational times every moment after 0 has t, t/2, t/4, ... below it). Denying H2 everywhere (fce4ac74) forbids a contingent concrete thing to be present at a non-initial moment of dense time in any accessible history. That anti-continuum commitment is paid by this side; A3 prime's own founded-past condition has it too. Control 8 (dense time with a first moment) satisfies A3, inert emptiness and universal coming-to-be while H2 holds and every bridge fails. H2 replacement accounts: a beginningless succession, each contingent thing preceded and grounded by an earlier one (control 3), or a continuous past with a first moment (control 8). H2 FINDINGS. (a) One derivation with independent content (populatedPastsFoundedOfStateFinitism, result 353e61b0): modal event-based finitism over momentary states (9c314355, reusing FiniteDistinctAncestry) plus the explicit precedence-to-causation bridge (20e6c7df) gives founded populated pasts. No no-loops premise is needed. Each premise survives alone (controls 1 and 2). (b) The Grim Reaper formulation (populatedPastsFoundedOfReaper, result c7c9b6d4) is a declared near-transcription. The bridge's consequent is a closed proposition about Nat functions that never mentions the descent, the history or its moments, and IndexedSignalReaper.impossible refutes it, so the bridge f63cd425 is equivalent to founded populated pasts. It is a reformulation, not a support route. Rejected re-encoding: any bridge whose consequent asserts a Nat station system is refuted the same way. A finite-to-global form over Nat functions is already refuted as mathematics (GrimReaperFiniteTests). A genuine patchwork premise needs a world-assembly vocabulary the corpus lacks. So H2 is excluded under the open finitism and precedence bridges only. H1 FINDINGS. Replacement account: a contingent thing with no earlier absence (an initial or sempiternal state) whose ground was not present before it. possiblyFoundedOfEarlierGrounds (result 493090f2) derives A3 prime from founded populated pasts and 6dd276f0 (possibly, a populated history in which every contingent concrete thing has an existing concrete ground present before each moment of its presence). A never-generated thing would be present at a moment with nothing earlier, where no ground can have been present before it. Rejecting GroundsPrecedeAt means only that some ground is not earlier: simultaneous (controls 4 and 5), only later (control 7: Nat time, x present only at 0, y from 1 on, each grounding the other, no edge between simultaneously present individuals), or never present. The grounding relation carries no temporal-presence constraint, so rejection does not imply simultaneous grounding. A sustaining ground present at all times satisfies GroundsPrecedeAt only for a grounded thing never present at a moment with nothing earlier; at an initial moment it fails (control 4). DISCLOSURE: possiblyNecessaryOfEarlierGrounds (result ca191c12) proves that founded populated pasts and 6dd276f0 entail that possibly a necessary concrete individual exists (d2d7cf61). Acc induction descends along earlier grounds to a non-contingent concrete ground. Under F1 and F2 this gives the stage-one conclusion at the selected world. So this A3 prime support bundle already carries the possibility of the target, and a rival who denies that a necessary concrete being is possible rejects 6dd276f0 (or fce4ac74) outright, whatever it says about H1. Without a necessary being, any rival keeping every contingent thing grounded must accept non-well-founded grounding (controls 5 and 7), the horn BruteFoundationBoundary.bruteRootOrNonWellFounded already forces; with well-founded grounding it gets a brute contingent root. PRICES for the initial-state rival who denies a necessary concrete being. On H2: reject state-causal finitism or the precedence bridge; these commitments also exclude dense-time histories with contingent things after the first moment. On H1: a brute contingent thing, or a ground with no earlier presence plus non-well-founded grounding. Neither price is called unreasonable here. Nothing is attributed to Koons, Pruss or any source. No premise is established.
blocker: All new premises are OPEN, and the H1 bundle already entails the possibility of a necessary concrete being, so it does not discriminate against a rival who denies that possibility. Next tests: (1) move foundedness from moments to discrete events or states, so that a continuous past with a first moment is not excluded, and compare with A3 prime; (2) a patchwork vocabulary over accessible worlds, so that a Reaper bridge can have content independent of founded pasts; (3) weaken the precedence bridge to some earlier state per populated moment; (4) find an H1 price that does not already entail possible necessary being, for example requiring only that grounds of contingent things are not later than them; (5) BoundedPastResource.noUniformGrowth as an independent price on H2.
